title: Mouse-derived Synaptosomes Trypsin Cleavage Assay to Characterize Synaptic Protein Sub-localization
author: Jasmeet Kaur Shergill
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Mouse ( Mus musculus , C57BL/6J) brain (preferably P60 or above) Reagents
Disodium hydrogen phosphate (Na 2 HPO 4 ) (ROTH, catalog number: T876.
Potassium dihydrogen phosphate (KH 2 PO 4 ) (ROTH, catalog number: 3904.
ROTIPHORSE Gel 30 (37.5:1), ready-to-use acrylamide (ROTH, catalog number: 3029.
Bovine serum albumin fraction V (BSA) (Sigma-Aldrich, catalog number: 1.12018.

steps.title: Sacrifice mice and dissect brains
steps.instruction: Cervically dislocate two C57BL/6J mice (≥P60) and immediately dissect each brain, keeping each brain in a separate tube.

steps.title: Homogenize brain tissue
steps.instruction: Place each brain in a pre‑chilled tissue‑grinding pestle, add 8 mL ice‑cold sucrose buffer (0.32 M sucrose, 5 mM HEPES, pH 8.0) and homogenize at 900 rpm with 12 up‑and‑down strokes.

steps.title: Transfer homogenate
steps.instruction: Move the homogenate to a 15 mL Falcon centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Remove large debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 900 × g for 10 min at 4 °C; keep the supernatant (S1) and discard the pellet (P1).

steps.title: Collect supernatant S1
steps.instruction: Transfer S1 to a new 15 mL tube.

steps.title: Pellet synaptosomal fraction
steps.instruction: Spin S1 at 10,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet P2
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant (S2) and gently pipette the pellet (P2) up‑and‑down 3–4 times in 2 mL ice‑cold sucrose buffer.

steps.title: Dilute pellet
steps.instruction: Add 6 mL ice‑cold sucrose buffer to the resuspended pellet and gently invert to mix.

steps.title: High‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 15,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend crude synaptosomes
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant (S2’) and resuspend the pellet (P2’, crude synaptosomes) in 2 mL sucrose buffer.

steps.title: Combine synaptosome preparations
steps.instruction: Pool the crude synaptosome suspensions from the two brains to obtain a total of 4 mL in a single 15 mL tube.

steps.title: Prepare Bradford reagent
steps.instruction: Mix the Bradford reagent thoroughly, allow it to reach room temperature before use.

steps.title: Prepare BSA protein standards
steps.instruction: Using the 2 mg/mL BSA stock in sucrose buffer, prepare the dilution series shown in Table 1 (e.g., 300 µL stock for 2 mg/mL, 370 µL stock +125 µL buffer for 1.5 mg/mL, etc.) to generate standards ranging from 0 to 2 mg/mL.

steps.title: Add Bradford reagent to wells
steps.instruction: Dispense 200 µL Bradford reagent into each well of a 96‑well plate, add 2 µL of each protein standard or of the crude synaptosome sample, mix; perform each measurement in triplicate.

steps.title: Incubate assay
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate for 5 min at room temperature in the dark.

steps.title: Measure absorbance
steps.instruction: Read absorbance at 595 nm using a SpectroStar Nano V5.70 plate reader.

steps.title: Calculate protein concentration
steps.instruction: Generate a standard curve and determine sample concentrations with MARS software (expected 2–3 mg/mL per mouse brain).

steps.title: Prepare untreated control
steps.instruction: Add 5 mg crude synaptosomes to 10 mL ice‑cold sucrose buffer (no trypsin).

steps.title: Prepare trypsin‑treated sample
steps.instruction: Add 5 mg crude synaptosomes to 10 mL ice‑cold sucrose buffer and add 500 µL trypsin solution (0.1 mg/mL) to obtain a protein‑to‑protease ratio of 100:1.

steps.title: Incubate digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate both tubes for 10 min at 30 °C in a water bath, gently inverting occasionally (no vortexing).

steps.title: Pellet proteins after digestion
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 8,700 × g for 3 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Stop protease activity
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 1 mL sucrose buffer containing 200 µL 6× loading sample buffer (final 5 µg/µL protein).

steps.title: Denature samples
steps.instruction: Boil the samples at 95 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Optional storage
steps.instruction: If not proceeding immediately, store samples at –20 °C (stable for at least three months).

steps.title: Clean casting plates
steps.instruction: Thoroughly clean the glass plates and insert them into the gel‑casting frame.

steps.title: Prepare separating gel solution
steps.instruction: In a 15 mL tube combine 3 mL water, 1.875 mL 4× separating buffer, 2.5 mL 30% acrylamide/bis‑acrylamide, 150 µL 10% APS, and 15 µL TEMED; swirl gently.

steps.title: Cast separating gel
steps.instruction: Pipette the separating gel between the plates, leaving ~2 cm space at the top.

steps.title: Overlay with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add isopropanol on top of the separating gel to flatten the surface.

steps.title: Remove overlay and dry
steps.instruction: After the gel polymerizes, pour off the isopropanol and let the gel dry for 5 min.

steps.title: Prepare stacking gel solution
steps.instruction: In a new 15 mL tube combine 1.625 mL water, 0.625 mL 4× stacking buffer, 0.333 mL 30% acrylamide/bis‑acrylamide, 75 µL 10% APS, and 7.5 µL TEMED; swirl gently.

steps.title: Cast stacking gel
steps.instruction: Pipette the stacking gel onto the set separating gel.

steps.title: Insert comb and set
steps.instruction: Place the comb carefully (avoid bubbles) and let the stacking gel polymerize for 10 min.

steps.title: Remove comb
steps.instruction: Carefully extract the comb once the stacking gel is fully set.

steps.title: Assemble gel in running apparatus
steps.instruction: Remove the gel from the casting stand, place it in the gel‑running cell, and fill inner and outer chambers with 1× running buffer.

steps.title: Load samples and ladder
steps.instruction: Load 20–30 µg of each untreated and trypsin‑treated sample plus a protein ladder into the wells.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Run at 80 V for the stacking phase (~40 min), then increase to 130 V for the resolving phase until the dye front reaches the bottom of the gel.

steps.title: Soak transfer materials
steps.instruction: Immerse the sponge, blotting paper, and nitrocellulose membrane in cold 1× transfer buffer.

steps.title: Assemble transfer sandwich
steps.instruction: Layer in order: sponge – blotting paper – nitrocellulose membrane – blotting paper – sponge.

steps.title: Remove air bubbles
steps.instruction: Roll a roller over the sandwich to eliminate trapped air.

steps.title: Fill transfer chamber
steps.instruction: Add cold 1× transfer buffer to the chamber and place a cool pack to keep the temperature low.

steps.title: Perform protein transfer
steps.instruction: Insert the sandwich and run the transfer at 110 V for 100 min in a cold room or with the chamber on ice.

steps.title: Stain membrane with Ponceau S
steps.instruction: Immediately after transfer, stain the nitrocellulose membrane with 0.5 % Ponceau S solution for a few minutes.

steps.title: Rinse and image membrane
steps.instruction: Rinse the membrane with water, capture an image of the stained bands.

steps.title: Remove Ponceau stain
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane repeatedly with 1× PBST until all stain is gone.

steps.title: Block membrane
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane in blocking solution (50 % Li‑COR blocking buffer + 50 % PBST) for 30–60 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare primary antibody solution
steps.instruction: Dilute each primary antibody in blocking solution according to Table 4 (e.g., GluR1 1:1,000, GluR2 1:1,000, GluN2A 1:200, GluN2B 1:200, Synaptotagmin1 1:500, Synaptophysin1 1:500, SNAP‑25 1:500).

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibody
steps.instruction: Place the membrane in the primary antibody solution and incubate overnight at 4 °C on a rotator.

steps.title: Wash after primary incubation
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane 3 × 10 min with 1× PBST at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare secondary antibody solution
steps.instruction: Dilute the appropriate IRDye secondary antibody (goat anti‑Rabbit 800 CW or goat anti‑Mouse 680 RD) 1:10,000 in 1× PBST.

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with secondary antibody for 45 min–1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Final washes
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane 3 × 10 min with 1× PBST, then 2 ×  with 1× PBS.

steps.title: Image blot
steps.instruction: Detect the proteins using the Li‑COR imaging system.

description: Validation of protocol To our knowledge, this protocol or parts of it has been used and validated in the following research articles: Boyken et al. [1]. Molecular Profiling of Synaptic Vesicle Docking Sites Reveals Novel Proteins but Few Differences between Glutamatergic and GABAergic Synapses. Neuron ( Figure 1 , panel B; Figure 2 , panel A). The protocol was originally developed for the isolation of a fraction highly enriched in synaptic vesicles docked to active zone. Mild proteolysis of synaptosomes was used to dissociate the presynaptic from the postsynaptic membrane. Awasthi et al. [17]. Synaptotagmin-3 drives AMPA receptor endocytosis, depression of synapse strength, and forgetting. Science ( Figure 1 , panel E and F). The protocol was used to verify the subcellular localization of synaptotagmin-3 (Syt-3). Awasthi et al. demonstrated that presynaptic proteins (such as synapsin, synaptobrevin-2, and Rab3a) were protected from trypsin cleavage, while postsynaptic proteins (such as Homer, GluA1, and PSD95), including Syt3, were cleaved. Azarnia Tehran et al. [18]. Selective endocytosis of Ca 2+ -permeable AMPARs by the Alzheimer’s disease risk factor CALM bidirectionally controls synaptic plasticity. Science Advances ( Figure 1 , panel B and C). The protocol was used to reveal the subcellular localization of the endocytic adaptor clathrin assembly lymphoid myeloid leukemia protein (CALM). We consistently found that while presynaptic proteins (such as SNAP-25, synaptophysin, and Rab3a) were protected from proteolysis, CALM was sensitive to trypsin, indicative of a large postsynaptic pool. Li et al. [20]. P85S6K sustains synaptic GluA1 to ameliorate cognitive deficits in Alzheimer’s disease. Translational Neurodegeneration ( Figure 1 , panel C). The protocol was used to verify the subcellular localization of p85S6K. As expected, presynaptic proteins (such as synaptophysin) were protected, while postsynaptic proteins (such as GluA1 and PSD95) were cleaved. Li et al
